data.name: Cmd.ls.Summary
data.value: List the files and folders in a folder

data.name: Cmd.ls.Details
data.value:
Lists what is inside a folder. Without a path it lists the folder you are in.
-a also show hidden files (names starting with a dot) -l long format: permissions, owner, size and date
Flags can be combined: 'ls -la' shows everything in long format.

data.name: Cmd.ls.Example2
data.value: Include hidden files

data.name: Cmd.ls.Example3
data.value: Everything in /var/www, in long format

data.name: Cmd.cd.Summary
data.value: Change directory – move into another folder

data.name: Cmd.cd.Details
data.value:
Moves you into another folder.
cd <folder> move into a folder cd .. go up one level cd ~ go back to your home folder (so does plain 'cd') cd / go to the very top of the file system (the root)

data.name: Cmd.pwd.Summary
data.value: Print working directory – show where you are

data.name: Cmd.pwd.Details
data.value: Shows the full path of the folder you are in right now. Paths starting with / are absolute: they start at the very top of the file system.

data.name: Cmd.pwd.Example1
data.value: Show the current folder

data.name: Cmd.cat.Summary
data.value: Show what is inside a file

data.name: Cmd.cat.Details
data.value:
Prints the contents of one or more files. The name is short for 'concatenate' – it can glue several files together.
-n number every line

data.name: Cmd.cat.Example1
data.value: Show notes.txt

data.name: Cmd.cat.Example2
data.value: Show /etc/passwd with line numbers

data.name: Cmd.grep.Summary
data.value: Search for text inside files

data.name: Cmd.grep.Details
data.value:
Prints every line that contains the text you are looking for. Perfect for digging through big log files.
-i ignore upper and lower case -n show line numbers -v invert: show the lines that do NOT match -r search every file in a folder and its subfolders
You can also send the output of another command into grep with a pipe (|).

data.name: Cmd.grep.Example3
data.value: Search every file under /home for 'password', in any case

data.name: Cmd.grep.Example4
data.value: Send a file through a pipe into grep

data.name: Cmd.find.Summary
data.value: Search for files and folders by name

data.name: Cmd.find.Details
data.value:
Searches through folders for files and folders.
find <name> quick search everywhere for names containing <name> find <path> -name <pat> search below <path>; * matches anything, ? one character -iname <pat> like -name, but ignores upper and lower case -type f / -type d only files / only folders
Folders you are not allowed to open are reported as 'Permission denied'.

data.value: Find hidden files in your home folder

data.name: Cmd.su.Summary
data.value: Switch user – become someone else (if you know the password)

data.name: Cmd.su.Details
data.value:
Lets you act as another user. You have to type that user's password; the letters are not shown while you type. Without a name, su tries to become root.
su lt;user gt; become lt;user gt; and stay in the same folder su - lt;user gt; become lt;user gt; and go to their home folder exit go back to the user you were before
On a real computer you may only do this with permission – just like everything else in Hackdot.

data.value: Go back to the user you were before su

data.name: Cmd.exit.Details
data.value: After switching user with su, exit takes you back to the user you were before – and to the folder you were in.
